decisions.mark: names MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the gating macros
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out (`include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787`). `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` (line 2196) and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` (line 2185) are also off." and "Enabling `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` plus `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` (or an ALT implementation) turns on the locks" | WHY: The answer names both macros and states that enabling them turns on the locking, which identifies them as the gating macros.

decisions.mark: states that the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves BOTH threading macros undefined, so a default build defines neither
decisions.detail: QUOTE: `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` is commented out (`include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787`). `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` (line 2196) and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_ALT` (line 2185) are also off. | WHY: The answer says the shipped config.h has THREADING_C commented out and PTHREAD and ALT also off, so a default build defines none of them.

decisions.mark: concludes that a default build of mbedtls creates no threads at all, and that the pthread example compiles to a stub main under that condition
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says the library never creates threads and THREADING_C is off by default, but it never mentions a pthread example compiling to a stub main.

decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "It never creates threads, so it runs concurrently only when your application calls it from several threads." | WHY: The answer says the library creates no threads, but it never says library/ supplies the mutex abstraction for threaded callers. It says threading.c compiles to nothing by default and that locks are compiled out, which is the opposite emphasis.
